report.source_text: At admission, the examination of the cheek revealed two nodules one centimeter in diameter, and another two centimeters in diameter with overlying erythematous skin and negative thermotouch. The nodules had a hard-elastic consistency, were moderately firm, and were not fluctuant. No associated lymphadenopathy was observed. The girl was afebrile and in a good general condition.

report.source_text: A histologic evaluation of a biopsy specimen of the largest nodule revealed an inflammatory, granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate in the superficial and deep dermis consisting of giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells (Figure 1). The Ziehl–Neelsen and Gram stains were both negative. The cultures for the anaerobic and aerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli were negative, as they were the antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented with two asymptomatic nodules on the left cheek convexity that appeared 2 months prior and gradually enlarged. Initial treatment with amoxicillin-clavulanate failed, suggesting non-infectious etiology. Physical examination revealed two nodules (1 cm and 2 cm diameter) with hard-elastic consistency, erythematous overlying skin, negative thermotouch, and no systemic signs (afebrile, good general condition, no lymphadenopathy). Ultrasound showed homogenous, hypoechoic, solid lesions. Histopathology of the largest nodule demonstrated granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate in the superficial and deep dermis with giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells. Negative Ziehl-Neelsen and Gram stains, negative cultures for anaerobic/aerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli, and negative serology for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis ruled out infectious etiologies. Treatment with topical fusidic acid and oral clarithromycin for 14 days was initiated. Complete resolution of lesions occurred within 2 months of first evaluation with no recurrence at 3-month follow-up.
